facts.text: The 30% AlFeNiCoCr-binder ZrB2 cermet was spark-plasma-sintered at 1300, 1400, 1500, or 1600 °C to identify the optimum sintering temperature.
Molten-aluminum corrosion was tested at 700 °C for 4, 8, or 12 days.
Ball-on-disc wear testing used a Si3N4 ball at room temperature, a 10 N load, 500 r/min, and a 30 min duration.
At 1500 °C, the liquid high-entropy-alloy binder uniformly filled pores and strongly connected the ZrB2 grains, producing a compact microstructure.
At 1600 °C, overflow and loss of the binder generated additional pores and weakened grain bonding.
The cermet sintered at 1500 °C had the highest relative density among the four sintering-temperature conditions.
The relative density of the 1500 °C cermet was 97.71%.
The 1500 °C cermet had the greatest fracture toughness among the tested sintering-temperature conditions and exceeded pure ZrB2.
After 12 days in molten aluminum, the 1500 °C cermet had a lower average corrosion rate than the cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C.
The detailed results reported a 12-day average corrosion rate of 1.225 × 10^-3 mm/h for the 1500 °C cermet.
The 1500 °C cermet had the lowest wear volume among the four sintering-temperature conditions.
The wear volume of the 1500 °C cermet was 0.104 mm^3.
